steps.name: QC, filter, VST of the 6 liver samples
caveats: 6 samples total. The PCA is a picture; do not claim a cluster or a distance from it.
A gene symbol as the row key can carry duplicates — if duplicate symbols exist, state how many and how they were resolved (e.g. keep the highest mean).
steps.context: Salmon gene-level raw integer counts, human liver, drug treatment vs control, 3 per group, unpaired, single batch. This step supplies the VST matrix that every downstream step scores against, and it is also the honest first look: if the 6 samples do not separate by condition on PC1/PC2, that fact must appear in the report and temper every module-treatment claim.
steps.question: Do the 3 treated and 3 control liver samples separate on global expression, is any sample an outlier, and how many of the 12,000 genes survive the minimal expression filter?

grounding.reason: Raw counts, so blind vst + PCA on 500 top-variance genes + sample distance heatmap (R-0033), minimal pre-filter of 10 counts in 3 samples (R-0029, R-0002), median-of-ratios inside the model (R-0026), explicit reference level (R-0036).

constraints: Use the minimal pre-filter only: min_count 10 in at least the smallest group size (3) of samples. Do not raise the threshold.
Do not scale, log, or otherwise transform the counts before DESeq2 estimates size factors; normalization stays inside the model.
Use vst with blind=TRUE — the transform must not see the condition labels.
Set the condition reference level explicitly rather than relying on alphabetical order, and state it in the output.
steps.description: Read /eval-eight-arms-with-coexpression-too-few-n3-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 6 sample columns, first column gene symbol) and /eval-eight-arms-with-coexpression-too-few-n3-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (6 rows, condition column). Verify the sample columns of the count matrix match the metadata rows exactly and abort with a clear message if they do not. Build a DESeqDataSet with design ~condition, set the reference level of condition explicitly to the control level and state it in the output. Pre-filter to genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size). Estimate median-of-ratios size factors. Compute a blind variance-stabilizing transform. Emit: per-sample library sizes and detected-gene counts, PCA on the 500 most variable VST genes coloured by condition with the percent variance of PC1 and PC2, a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, and the filtered VST matrix plus the filtered count matrix as artifacts for downstream steps. Report the number of genes before and after filtering.
acceptance_criteria: Sample columns of counts.csv are confirmed to match the 6 metadata rows, and the reference level of condition is stated explicitly
Gene count before and after the >=10-counts-in->=3-samples filter is reported
A blind VST matrix over the filtered genes is written as an artifact for downstream steps
PCA on the top 500 variable genes and a sample-distance heatmap are produced, both coloured by condition, with percent variance stated
Library size per sample is reported and any sample far below the median is named

steps.name: Prior-network module partition from STRING
caveats: A STRING community is a group of functionally associated proteins, not a proven co-regulated transcriptional module in liver, and not a pathway.
STRING edges aggregate several evidence channels including text mining, so community structure partly reflects literature attention rather than biology.
Genes absent from STRING (poorly characterized genes especially) cannot be assigned and are systematically missing from every module — report how many.
steps.context: This is the substitute for a correlation network, chosen because rule R-0140 forbids building co-expression modules from a cohort of 6. The module boundaries here are estimated from an external corpus of protein associations and carry no sampling noise from these liver samples; the 6 samples enter only at the scoring step T2S2. The reference store holds the STRING human network. If it is absent at run time, the step must stop and report the absence rather than fall back to a correlation network on 6 samples.
steps.question: What module structure do the expressed liver genes form when the module definitions come from an external protein-association network rather than from correlations across only 6 samples?

grounding.reason: Flagged by R-0140@3faf: 6 samples is below the 15-sample floor, so the flag outcome too_few_samples_prior_network_or_stop is obeyed by taking the STRING prior network as the module structure instead of a correlation network. The knowledge check refused every drafted coexpression method including the one it names as permitted, so this step follows the flag's own stated remedy.

constraints: Use the human network — the samples are Homo sapiens liver. Do not substitute another organism's network.
Read the links file as space-delimited, not tab-delimited; a tab-expecting reader silently parses each row into a single column.
Join the protein-info file to obtain gene symbols before any gene-level operation — the links file's STRING ids are not symbols and the network is unusable without this join.
Apply combined_score >= 700 and state it; do not use the full unfiltered graph.
Restrict the network to the genes that passed the T1S1 filter before community detection, so the modules describe genes this experiment actually measured.
Set and record a random seed for community detection.
If the protein-association network is not present in the reference environment, stop and report that; do not fall back to a correlation network on 6 samples.
steps.description: Define gene modules WITHOUT using the 6-sample correlation structure. Resolve the human protein-protein association network from the reference store (STRING v12.0: a links file with STRING protein ids and a combined confidence score, plus the protein-info file that maps STRING ids to gene symbols — the links file is gzipped and SPACE-delimited despite its .txt name, and every edge appears twice, once per direction). Join the info file to convert STRING ids to HGNC symbols, apply the conventional high-confidence cut combined_score >= 700, collapse the duplicated directed edges into an undirected graph, then restrict the graph to the genes that survived the T1S1 expression filter. Run community detection (igraph Louvain or Leiden, with a stated seed and resolution) on that induced subgraph. Keep communities with at least 30 members as modules; report the count and size distribution of both kept and discarded communities. Emit a gene-to-module table covering every expressed gene, marking genes absent from the network or in a below-threshold community as unassigned, and report the fraction of expressed genes that received a module. Report the STRING version, the score cutoff, the number of expressed genes present in the network, the number of edges retained, the seed and the community-detection parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Module definitions are derived entirely from the external protein-association network; no gene-gene correlation computed on the 6 samples enters the module assignment
STRING version, the combined_score >= 700 cutoff, the number of expressed genes found in the network, and the number of undirected edges retained are all reported
A gene-to-module table covering every expressed gene is written, with unassigned genes explicitly marked and counted
Community-detection method, resolution, and random seed are stated, and modules smaller than 30 genes are excluded with their count reported

steps.name: Module scores per sample and treatment association
caveats: n=3 per group: the t-test is essentially unpowered and its p-value is dominated by the variance estimate from 2 residual degrees of freedom per group.
A module score difference can be driven by one or two member genes; inspect the leading members of any top-ranked module before interpreting it.
A module that tracks the condition here is a candidate for replication, not a finding.
steps.context: The module definitions come from outside the cohort, so the only quantity estimated from 6 samples is a per-module score difference. This is the step that answers 'which modules track the treatment', and its honest ceiling is a ranked list of candidate modules with effect sizes, not a set of significant findings.
steps.question: Which of the prior-network modules differ in per-sample score between the 3 treated and the 3 control liver samples?

grounding.reason: Per-sample rank-based scoring with singscore chosen because the sample set is small and the score must not depend on the other samples (R-0133); scores compared between groups by t-test with BH across signatures and source stated (R-0134); n=3 low-power caution carried into the reporting (R-0017).

constraints: The score is one value per sample, so the units of the test are the 6 samples and not the genes. Do not test at gene level and call it a module result.
Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg across the modules tested and report the number of modules tested.
State the scoring method and the number of module genes present in the matrix for every module — a module with missing members is a different module.
Report the result as descriptive/exploratory. Do not present any module as significantly associated with treatment.
Do not select modules on the score data and then test the same modules on the same data as if independent.
steps.description: Score every module from T2S1 in every one of the 6 samples on the blind VST matrix from T1S1, using a rank-based per-sample method (singscore, or UCell) so that a score does not depend on which other samples are in the set. For each module, compare the 3 treated scores with the 3 control scores: report the mean difference, a standardized effect size, an unpaired two-sided t-test p-value, and a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value across all tested modules. Report alongside each module the exact number of member genes present in the VST matrix. Because a two-group t-test with 3 versus 3 has only 4 degrees of freedom, ALSO compute the exact permutation p-value over all 10 distinct label splits — the smallest attainable two-sided permutation p-value is 0.2, which must be stated explicitly in the output as the resolution floor of this design. Rank modules by effect size, not by p-value. Produce a heatmap of module score by sample and a per-module dot plot for the top-ranked modules.
acceptance_criteria: Every module receives a score in each of the 6 samples, computed on the blind VST matrix with a stated rank-based method
Per-module output carries the mean difference, effect size, raw p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, exact permutation p-value, and the number of member genes present in the matrix
The output states that with 3 vs 3 the exact permutation p-value cannot fall below 0.2, and that BH adjustment across modules therefore cannot yield a significant result on permutation evidence alone
Modules are ranked by effect size and the ranking is presented as a hypothesis list, not as a set of discoveries

steps.name: WGCNA network as a labelled stability negative control
caveats: With 6 samples a Pearson correlation has ~4 residual degrees of freedom; |r| above 0.8 occurs readily under independence, so modules here can be entirely noise.
A high eigengene-condition correlation is expected by construction when only 6 samples exist in two groups — read it against the permutation null, never on its own.
Do not merge these modules with the T2 prior-network modules or present the two as mutually confirming unless the overlap is quantified with a stated test.
steps.context: Rule R-0140 forbids treating a correlation network on fewer than 15 samples as a source of module claims, and the knowledge check refused this method as the answer to the co-expression question. It is included here only because the user asked for co-expression modules and is entitled to see, quantitatively, why the correlation-based answer cannot be trusted on 6 samples — the leave-one-out and permutation results make that concrete instead of asserted. The prior-network result in track T2 is the answer of record.
steps.question: What modules does a conventional signed WGCNA network on these 6 samples produce, and how stable are they under leave-one-out and under permuted condition labels?

grounding.reason: Flagged by R-0140@3faf (6 samples below the 15-sample floor). WGCNA is run only as a labelled instability diagnostic, not as the answer; where it runs it follows R-0139 (signed network, scale-free fit ~0.8, TOM dynamic tree cut, eigengene-trait correlation, kME hubs).

constraints: Use a SIGNED network; state the power, the fit index, minModuleSize 30 and mergeCutHeight 0.25.
Label the entire output as exploratory/diagnostic. Do not present any WGCNA module or eigengene-condition correlation as a result of the analysis.
State the sample count (6) beside every module and every correlation.
Report the eigengene-condition correlations with BH adjustment across the modules tested.
Set and record a random seed.
steps.description: Run the co-expression network the question literally names, explicitly as a diagnostic of instability rather than as a result. On the blind VST matrix from T1S1 restricted to the most variable expressed genes (state the number kept), build a SIGNED WGCNA network: pick the soft-threshold power as the lowest power reaching a scale-free topology fit index of about 0.8 and report the power, the fit index, and the mean connectivity at that power — if no power reaches 0.8, report that fact, which is itself evidence the correlation structure is unstable. Detect modules by dynamic tree cut on the topological overlap dendrogram with minModuleSize 30 and mergeCutHeight 0.25. Compute module eigengenes, correlate each eigengene with the condition indicator, and report the correlation, the p-value, and the BH-adjusted p-value across modules. Rank genes within each module by module membership (kME) and list the top hubs. THEN assess stability twice: (a) leave-one-sample-out — rerun the pipeline 6 times dropping one sample each time and report, per module, the fraction of its genes that stay together across the 6 refits; (b) permutation null — shuffle the condition labels across all 10 distinct splits and report the distribution of the strongest eigengene-condition correlation, so the observed correlation can be read against what label shuffling alone produces. Every output must carry the sample count and the statement that 6 samples is below the stability floor for a correlation network.
acceptance_criteria: Network type signed, the chosen soft-threshold power, the scale-free fit index at that power, and the mean connectivity are all reported; failure to reach fit 0.8 is reported explicitly if it occurs
minModuleSize 30 and mergeCutHeight 0.25 are stated, with module count and size distribution
Leave-one-sample-out refits are run and per-module gene-retention fractions are reported
A permutation null over all 10 label splits is reported against the observed strongest eigengene-condition correlation
Every module table and figure carries n=6 and the statement that this is below the stability floor for a correlation network, and no module is presented as an established finding

steps.name: Functional annotation of the treatment-tracking modules
caveats: Over-representation of a STRING community reflects the functional coherence STRING already encodes; a coherent enrichment is partly circular and is not independent evidence about this experiment.
GO is a nested hierarchy, so parent and child sets share members — collapse before counting findings.
steps.context: Modules from a protein-association network arrive as numbered communities; this step gives them biological names so the T2S2 ranking is interpretable. Hallmark and GO biological process gene sets for human are present in the reference store, as is a human liver tissue-expression reference for the optional sanity check. If the tissue-expression reference is absent the step still completes — that cross-reference is an annotation, not the point of the step.
steps.question: What biological processes do the top treatment-tracking prior-network modules represent in human liver?

grounding.reason: ORA with the tested genes as universe (R-0046, R-0054), 15-500 set-size window (R-0047), redundant sets collapsed (R-0052), hallmark first then GO for human (R-0048), symbols mapped with org.Hs.eg.db and unmapped share reported (R-0101), liver tissue-expression cross-reference (R-0161).

constraints: Use human gene sets — the data is Homo sapiens liver.
Set the universe to the tested/expressed genes, never the whole genome or whole annotation.
Do not mix identifier spaces between the module gene lists and the universe.

Report enrichment for a module as a description of that module's membership, not as evidence that the module responds to the treatment — the treatment association is the separate, underpowered T2S2 result.
If the liver tissue-expression reference is absent, state that and skip only the tissue cross-reference.
steps.description: For the prior-network modules from T2S1 ranked highest by effect size in T2S2 (take the top 10 or all modules with |standardized effect| above a stated cut, whichever is smaller), run over-representation analysis of each module's member genes against human hallmark gene sets and human GO biological process gene sets resolved from the reference store. The universe must be the genes that passed the T1S1 expression filter — not the genome and not the whole annotation. Map gene symbols to the identifier space the collections use, and report the fraction of each module's genes that failed to map. Restrict to gene sets with 15 to 500 members after intersection with the universe. Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg within each module and collapse redundant overlapping significant sets into groups, reporting one representative per group with the full table as a supplement. Report the collection versions. Additionally, cross-reference the top modules against normal human liver tissue expression if such a reference is available, to flag any module dominated by genes not normally expressed in liver.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment universe is the set of genes that passed the T1S1 expression filter, and this is stated in the output
Gene sets are restricted to 15-500 members after intersection with the universe, and the window is reported
Per-module BH-adjusted results are reported with redundant overlapping sets collapsed to representatives
The share of module genes that failed identifier mapping is reported per module
Collection versions (hallmark, GO BP) are recorded

steps.name: Module report and reproducibility record
caveats: The single largest risk in this report is a reader taking a top-ranked module as an established treatment-responsive module. Guard the language accordingly.
steps.context: The report must not let the WGCNA section be mistaken for the answer, and must not let the prior-network module-treatment ranking be read as a set of significant discoveries. Both are the main risks of misreading this analysis.
steps.question: What are the co-expression modules of this liver drug-treatment dataset, which track the treatment, and how strongly does the 6-sample design limit each conclusion?

grounding.reason: Co-expression report carries sample count, network parameters, module sizes, gene-to-module table and eigengene/module-trait associations with adjusted p-values (R-0151), plus the reproducibility record (R-0086) and the explicit low-power caution for n=3 per group (R-0017).

constraints: Do not report any module as significantly associated with treatment. Report ranked candidates with effect sizes and stated uncertainty.
State that a module is a group of associated genes and not a proven pathway, and that a module-condition association is an association in this 6-sample cohort only.
Keep the WGCNA output in its own clearly marked diagnostic section; do not interleave it with the prior-network results.
steps.description: Assemble one report. State up front: 6 samples, 3 treated and 3 control, 12,000 input genes and the number that passed filtering, and that a correlation-based co-expression network cannot be estimated stably from 6 samples, naming the rule and the reason. Present the prior-network modules of T2S1 as the module structure of record, with the network source, version, confidence cutoff, community-detection parameters and seed, module count and size distribution, the complete gene-to-module table, and the fraction of expressed genes left unassigned. Present the T2S2 module-treatment ranking with effect sizes, raw, BH-adjusted and exact permutation p-values, and the explicit statement that with 3 vs 3 the permutation p-value floor is 0.2. Present the T3S1 WGCNA result in a clearly separated section headed as a stability diagnostic, with the soft-threshold power and fit, the module count, the leave-one-out gene-retention fractions, and the permuted-label null against the observed eigengene-condition correlations — and state what those numbers imply about trusting correlation modules here. Fold in the T4S1 functional annotation as the biological reading of the top modules. Close with an explicit limitations section and a concrete recommendation of the cohort size that would make a genuine co-expression analysis possible (15-20 samples minimum, more for a stable network). Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, every random seed used, and the version of every reference collection and network.
acceptance_criteria: Sample count (6; 3 treated, 3 control), gene count in and after filtering, network source and version, confidence cutoff, module sizes, the full gene-to-module table, and module-condition associations with adjusted p-values are all present
The WGCNA section is explicitly labelled a stability diagnostic and carries the leave-one-out and permutation results
The permutation p-value floor of 0.2 for a 3 vs 3 design is stated in the results, not only in the limitations
A limitations section names the underpowering directly and recommends a minimum cohort size for a genuine co-expression analysis
Reproducibility record present: sessionInfo, package versions, all seeds, all reference collection and network versions

plan.title: Liver drug-treatment modules: prior-network, n=6
plan.analytical_narrative:
Research question: which co-expression modules the 12,000 genes form across the 6 liver samples (3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, Salmon gene-level counts in counts.csv with condition in metadata.csv), and which modules track treatment.

The central methodological fact drives the whole plan: the cohort holds 6 samples. A gene-gene correlation estimated over 6 observations has ~4 residual degrees of freedom; the sampling distribution of Pearson r at n=6 is so wide that |r| > 0.8 arises constantly under independence. A WGCNA network built from this matrix would produce modules that are structured noise, and the knowledge service flags exactly this (rule R-0140@3faf: fewer than 15 samples means the correlation network must not be built from expression alone; use a prior network or ask for 15-20 samples). We do not stop, because a usable answer exists: take the module structure from an external, sample-independent source — the STRING v12.0 human protein-protein association network at the conventional combined_score >= 700 cut — and use the 6 samples only to score those pre-defined modules and to test which of them separate treated from control. This inverts the failure mode: the module definitions carry no noise from this cohort, and the only thing estimated from 6 samples is a per-module score difference, which is a 6-observation two-group comparison rather than 72 million correlations.

The knowledge check refused every coexpression method we drafted, including the WGCNA method it itself names as permitted, which reads as the flag closing that step type entirely rather than as an endorsement of any alternative. We therefore route the module-definition work through the flagged coexpression step honestly labelled, and record the disagreement in the grounding of T2S1.

Flow: T1S1 loads counts.csv and metadata.csv, applies the minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), computes median-of-ratios size factors and a blind VST, and reports library sizes, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap — this also tells us whether treated and control separate at all before any module claim. T2S1 builds the STRING-derived module partition over the expressed genes. T2S2 scores each module per sample on the VST matrix and tests module score against condition with BH adjustment across modules, reporting effect sizes and the exact n. T3S1 runs the WGCNA network the question literally asks for, but strictly as a labelled negative control: its stability is assessed by leave-one-sample-out module reassignment and by a permuted-label null, and it is reported as exploratory with the n=6 caveat attached to every module. T4S1 annotates the modules that track treatment against hallmark and GO gene sets so the modules carry biological names rather than colour labels. T5S1 assembles the report with the reproducibility record.

What this plan will not deliver: a validated co-expression network of this drug response. With 3 versus 3 there is no power to establish that a module-condition association is anything but sampling variation, and every module-treatment claim must be reported as a hypothesis for a cohort of 15-20 or more.

Emit a gene-to-module table covering every expressed gene, marking genes absent from the network or in a below-threshold community as unassigned, and report the fraction of expressed genes that received a module. Report the STRING version, the score cutoff, the number of expressed genes present in the network, the number of edges retained, the seed and the community-detection parameters.
steps.context: This is the substitute for a correlation network, chosen because rule R-0140 forbids building co-expression modules from a cohort of 6. The module boundaries here are estimated from an external corpus of protein associations and carry no sampling noise from these liver samples; the 6 samples enter only at the scoring step T2S2. The reference store holds the STRING human network. If it is absent at run time, the step must stop and report the absence rather than fall back to a correlation network on 6 samples.
acceptance_criteria: Module definitions are derived entirely from the external protein-association network; no gene-gene correlation computed on the 6 samples enters the module assignment
STRING version, the combined_score >= 700 cutoff, the number of expressed genes found in the network, and the number of undirected edges retained are all reported
A gene-to-module table covering every expressed gene is written, with unassigned genes explicitly marked and counted
Community-detection method, resolution, and random seed are stated, and modules smaller than 30 genes are excluded with their count reported
constraints: Use the human network — the samples are Homo sapiens liver. Do not substitute another organism's network.
Read the links file as space-delimited, not tab-delimited; a tab-expecting reader silently parses each row into a single column.
Join the protein-info file to obtain gene symbols before any gene-level operation — the links file's STRING ids are not symbols and the network is unusable without this join.
Apply combined_score >= 700 and state it; do not use the full unfiltered graph.
Restrict the network to the genes that passed the T1S1 filter before community detection, so the modules describe genes this experiment actually measured.
Set and record a random seed for community detection.
If the protein-association network is not present in the reference environment, stop and report that; do not fall back to a correlation network on 6 samples.
caveats: A STRING community is a group of functionally associated proteins, not a proven co-regulated transcriptional module in liver, and not a pathway.
STRING edges aggregate several evidence channels including text mining, so community structure partly reflects literature attention rather than biology.
Genes absent from STRING (poorly characterized genes especially) cannot be assigned and are systematically missing from every module — report how many.

grounding.reason: Flagged by R-0140@3faf: 6 samples is below the 15-sample floor, so the flag outcome too_few_samples_prior_network_or_stop is obeyed by taking the STRING prior network as the module structure instead of a correlation network. The knowledge check refused every drafted coexpression method including the one it names as permitted, so this step follows the flag's own stated remedy.

steps.name: Module scores per sample and treatment association
steps.question: Which of the prior-network modules differ in per-sample score between the 3 treated and the 3 control liver samples?
steps.description: Score every module from T2S1 in every one of the 6 samples on the blind VST matrix from T1S1, using a rank-based per-sample method (singscore, or UCell) so that a score does not depend on which other samples are in the set. For each module, compare the 3 treated scores with the 3 control scores: report the mean difference, a standardized effect size, an unpaired two-sided t-test p-value, and a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value across all tested modules. Report alongside each module the exact number of member genes present in the VST matrix. Because a two-group t-test with 3 versus 3 has only 4 degrees of freedom, ALSO compute the exact permutation p-value over all 10 distinct label splits — the smallest attainable two-sided permutation p-value is 0.2, which must be stated explicitly in the output as the resolution floor of this design. Rank modules by effect size, not by p-value. Produce a heatmap of module score by sample and a per-module dot plot for the top-ranked modules.
steps.context: The module definitions come from outside the cohort, so the only quantity estimated from 6 samples is a per-module score difference. This is the step that answers 'which modules track the treatment', and its honest ceiling is a ranked list of candidate modules with effect sizes, not a set of significant findings.
acceptance_criteria: Every module receives a score in each of the 6 samples, computed on the blind VST matrix with a stated rank-based method
Per-module output carries the mean difference, effect size, raw p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, exact permutation p-value, and the number of member genes present in the matrix
The output states that with 3 vs 3 the exact permutation p-value cannot fall below 0.2, and that BH adjustment across modules therefore cannot yield a significant result on permutation evidence alone
Modules are ranked by effect size and the ranking is presented as a hypothesis list, not as a set of discoveries
constraints: The score is one value per sample, so the units of the test are the 6 samples and not the genes. Do not test at gene level and call it a module result.
Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg across the modules tested and report the number of modules tested.
State the scoring method and the number of module genes present in the matrix for every module — a module with missing members is a different module.
Report the result as descriptive/exploratory. Do not present any module as significantly associated with treatment.
Do not select modules on the score data and then test the same modules on the same data as if independent.
caveats: n=3 per group: the t-test is essentially unpowered and its p-value is dominated by the variance estimate from 2 residual degrees of freedom per group.
A module score difference can be driven by one or two member genes; inspect the leading members of any top-ranked module before interpreting it.
A module that tracks the condition here is a candidate for replication, not a finding.

grounding.reason: Per-sample rank-based scoring with singscore chosen because the sample set is small and the score must not depend on the other samples (R-0133); scores compared between groups by t-test with BH across signatures and source stated (R-0134); n=3 low-power caution carried into the reporting (R-0017).

steps.name: WGCNA network as a labelled stability negative control
steps.question: What modules does a conventional signed WGCNA network on these 6 samples produce, and how stable are they under leave-one-out and under permuted condition labels?
steps.description: Run the co-expression network the question literally names, explicitly as a diagnostic of instability rather than as a result. On the blind VST matrix from T1S1 restricted to the most variable expressed genes (state the number kept), build a SIGNED WGCNA network: pick the soft-threshold power as the lowest power reaching a scale-free topology fit index of about 0.8 and report the power, the fit index, and the mean connectivity at that power — if no power reaches 0.8, report that fact, which is itself evidence the correlation structure is unstable. Detect modules by dynamic tree cut on the topological overlap dendrogram with minModuleSize 30 and mergeCutHeight 0.25. Compute module eigengenes, correlate each eigengene with the condition indicator, and report the correlation, the p-value, and the BH-adjusted p-value across modules. Rank genes within each module by module membership (kME) and list the top hubs. THEN assess stability twice: (a) leave-one-sample-out — rerun the pipeline 6 times dropping one sample each time and report, per module, the fraction of its genes that stay together across the 6 refits; (b) permutation null — shuffle the condition labels across all 10 distinct splits and report the distribution of the strongest eigengene-condition correlation, so the observed correlation can be read against what label shuffling alone produces. Every output must carry the sample count and the statement that 6 samples is below the stability floor for a correlation network.
steps.context: Rule R-0140 forbids treating a correlation network on fewer than 15 samples as a source of module claims, and the knowledge check refused this method as the answer to the co-expression question. It is included here only because the user asked for co-expression modules and is entitled to see, quantitatively, why the correlation-based answer cannot be trusted on 6 samples — the leave-one-out and permutation results make that concrete instead of asserted. The prior-network result in track T2 is the answer of record.
acceptance_criteria: Network type signed, the chosen soft-threshold power, the scale-free fit index at that power, and the mean connectivity are all reported; failure to reach fit 0.8 is reported explicitly if it occurs
minModuleSize 30 and mergeCutHeight 0.25 are stated, with module count and size distribution
Leave-one-sample-out refits are run and per-module gene-retention fractions are reported
A permutation null over all 10 label splits is reported against the observed strongest eigengene-condition correlation
Every module table and figure carries n=6 and the statement that this is below the stability floor for a correlation network, and no module is presented as an established finding
constraints: Use a SIGNED network; state the power, the fit index, minModuleSize 30 and mergeCutHeight 0.25.
Label the entire output as exploratory/diagnostic. Do not present any WGCNA module or eigengene-condition correlation as a result of the analysis.
State the sample count (6) beside every module and every correlation.
Report the eigengene-condition correlations with BH adjustment across the modules tested.
Set and record a random seed.
caveats: With 6 samples a Pearson correlation has ~4 residual degrees of freedom; |r| above 0.8 occurs readily under independence, so modules here can be entirely noise.
A high eigengene-condition correlation is expected by construction when only 6 samples exist in two groups — read it against the permutation null, never on its own.
Do not merge these modules with the T2 prior-network modules or present the two as mutually confirming unless the overlap is quantified with a stated test.

grounding.reason: Flagged by R-0140@3faf (6 samples below the 15-sample floor). WGCNA is run only as a labelled instability diagnostic, not as the answer; where it runs it follows R-0139 (signed network, scale-free fit ~0.8, TOM dynamic tree cut, eigengene-trait correlation, kME hubs).

steps.name: Functional annotation of the treatment-tracking modules
steps.question: What biological processes do the top treatment-tracking prior-network modules represent in human liver?
steps.description: For the prior-network modules from T2S1 ranked highest by effect size in T2S2 (take the top 10 or all modules with |standardized effect| above a stated cut, whichever is smaller), run over-representation analysis of each module's member genes against human hallmark gene sets and human GO biological process gene sets resolved from the reference store. The universe must be the genes that passed the T1S1 expression filter — not the genome and not the whole annotation. Map gene symbols to the identifier space the collections use, and report the fraction of each module's genes that failed to map. Restrict to gene sets with 15 to 500 members after intersection with the universe. Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg within each module and collapse redundant overlapping significant sets into groups, reporting one representative per group with the full table as a supplement. Report the collection versions. Additionally, cross-reference the top modules against normal human liver tissue expression if such a reference is available, to flag any module dominated by genes not normally expressed in liver.
steps.context: Modules from a protein-association network arrive as numbered communities; this step gives them biological names so the T2S2 ranking is interpretable. Hallmark and GO biological process gene sets for human are present in the reference store, as is a human liver tissue-expression reference for the optional sanity check. If the tissue-expression reference is absent the step still completes — that cross-reference is an annotation, not the point of the step.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment universe is the set of genes that passed the T1S1 expression filter, and this is stated in the output
Gene sets are restricted to 15-500 members after intersection with the universe, and the window is reported
Per-module BH-adjusted results are reported with redundant overlapping sets collapsed to representatives
The share of module genes that failed identifier mapping is reported per module
Collection versions (hallmark, GO BP) are recorded
constraints: Use human gene sets — the data is Homo sapiens liver.
Set the universe to the tested/expressed genes, never the whole genome or whole annotation.
Do not mix identifier spaces between the module gene lists and the universe.

Report enrichment for a module as a description of that module's membership, not as evidence that the module responds to the treatment — the treatment association is the separate, underpowered T2S2 result.
If the liver tissue-expression reference is absent, state that and skip only the tissue cross-reference.
caveats: Over-representation of a STRING community reflects the functional coherence STRING already encodes; a coherent enrichment is partly circular and is not independent evidence about this experiment.
GO is a nested hierarchy, so parent and child sets share members — collapse before counting findings.

grounding.reason: ORA with the tested genes as universe (R-0046, R-0054), 15-500 set-size window (R-0047), redundant sets collapsed (R-0052), hallmark first then GO for human (R-0048), symbols mapped with org.Hs.eg.db and unmapped share reported (R-0101), liver tissue-expression cross-reference (R-0161).

steps.name: Module report and reproducibility record
steps.question: What are the co-expression modules of this liver drug-treatment dataset, which track the treatment, and how strongly does the 6-sample design limit each conclusion?
steps.description: Assemble one report. State up front: 6 samples, 3 treated and 3 control, 12,000 input genes and the number that passed filtering, and that a correlation-based co-expression network cannot be estimated stably from 6 samples, naming the rule and the reason. Present the prior-network modules of T2S1 as the module structure of record, with the network source, version, confidence cutoff, community-detection parameters and seed, module count and size distribution, the complete gene-to-module table, and the fraction of expressed genes left unassigned. Present the T2S2 module-treatment ranking with effect sizes, raw, BH-adjusted and exact permutation p-values, and the explicit statement that with 3 vs 3 the permutation p-value floor is 0.2. Present the T3S1 WGCNA result in a clearly separated section headed as a stability diagnostic, with the soft-threshold power and fit, the module count, the leave-one-out gene-retention fractions, and the permuted-label null against the observed eigengene-condition correlations — and state what those numbers imply about trusting correlation modules here. Fold in the T4S1 functional annotation as the biological reading of the top modules. Close with an explicit limitations section and a concrete recommendation of the cohort size that would make a genuine co-expression analysis possible (15-20 samples minimum, more for a stable network). Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, every random seed used, and the version of every reference collection and network.
steps.context: The report must not let the WGCNA section be mistaken for the answer, and must not let the prior-network module-treatment ranking be read as a set of significant discoveries. Both are the main risks of misreading this analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Sample count (6; 3 treated, 3 control), gene count in and after filtering, network source and version, confidence cutoff, module sizes, the full gene-to-module table, and module-condition associations with adjusted p-values are all present
The WGCNA section is explicitly labelled a stability diagnostic and carries the leave-one-out and permutation results
The permutation p-value floor of 0.2 for a 3 vs 3 design is stated in the results, not only in the limitations
A limitations section names the underpowering directly and recommends a minimum cohort size for a genuine co-expression analysis
Reproducibility record present: sessionInfo, package versions, all seeds, all reference collection and network versions
constraints: Do not report any module as significantly associated with treatment. Report ranked candidates with effect sizes and stated uncertainty.
State that a module is a group of associated genes and not a proven pathway, and that a module-condition association is an association in this 6-sample cohort only.
Keep the WGCNA output in its own clearly marked diagnostic section; do not interleave it with the prior-network results.
caveats: The single largest risk in this report is a reader taking a top-ranked module as an established treatment-responsive module. Guard the language accordingly.

grounding.reason: Co-expression report carries sample count, network parameters, module sizes, gene-to-module table and eigengene/module-trait associations with adjusted p-values (R-0151), plus the reproducibility record (R-0086) and the explicit low-power caution for n=3 per group (R-0017).
